decision: Implement vision-based PDF extraction using pypdfium2 + GPT-4o for complex multi-column layouts
reason: Text-based extractors (pdfplumber, pypdf, pdfminer) all fail on side-by-side columns; vision is the only reliable method for pitch decks with non-standard layouts

decision: Use 'transcribe every word' prompt for vision extraction instead of 'identify people' to avoid OpenAI refusal
reason: GPT-4o refuses to identify people in photos; asking for raw text transcription bypasses the safety filter while still extracting names from text labels

decision: Accept 'D' prefix on Bippin's name as cosmetic noise from PDF avatar icon; do not strip it
reason: The 'D' is a circular icon in the PDF that gets transcribed as a letter; LLM will correctly ignore it when answering questions about founders; stripping adds complexity without user-visible benefit

decision: Use gpt-4o (not gpt-4o-mini) for PDF vision extraction with text-transcription-only prompt
reason: gpt-4o-mini triggers OpenAI's person-identification refusal policy when asked to identify people in images; gpt-4o with a text-only transcription prompt avoids the refusal and correctly extracts founder names

decision: Run KG traversal and Serper web search in parallel on every question, merge both contexts into LLM prompt
reason: Sequential search or fire-and-forget background jobs do not feed web context into the answer; parallel execution ensures both KG and web results inform the LLM response

decision: Save Q&A as new chunks in a conversation asset linked to the project, making answers traversable in future queries
reason: Answers must persist to the knowledge graph so subsequent questions can build on prior Q&A; fire-and-forget responses do not contribute to the KG

Use Haiku (not Claude 3.5 Sonnet) for intent classification to keep latency low and cost minimal
reason: Intent classification is a lightweight structured extraction task; Haiku is fast enough and reduces API cost per conversation turn

decision: Run KG traversal before intent classification so the judge has access to actual document chunks and can extract real entity names
reason: Generic search fails because it doesn't know the real founder names or company context; KG chunks provide ground truth for entity extraction

decision: Run targeted Serper queries and URL scraping in parallel after intent classification completes
reason: Parallelization keeps perceived latency low; both sources (web search + doc URLs) are valuable and can run simultaneously

decision: Display intent classification in left panel as IntentCard with intent sentence + search query tags
reason: Transparency: investor can see exactly what the assistant is searching for and why; builds trust in the system

decision: Extract URLs from KG chunks and scrape them as part of intent-driven search (not just Serper results)
reason: Pitch decks often contain founder LinkedIn profiles, company websites, and news coverage; scraping these is more reliable than generic web search for founder background

decision: Use Haiku (not Opus) for intent classification to keep latency low and cost reasonable; judge runs synchronously before Serper queries, so speed matters
reason: Intent classification is a lightweight task (read question + 2 KG chunks, output structured JSON); Haiku is fast enough and cheaper than Opus

decision: Judge reads top 2 KG chunks (sorted by relevance from traversal) instead of all chunks, capped at ~500 tokens total
reason: Reduces OCR noise and keeps judge focused on the most relevant document context; full chunk list would overwhelm judge with irrelevant text

decision: Judge output includes both `queries[]` (for Serper) and `urls[]` (for direct scraping) so web intelligence comes from two sources: targeted searches + document links
reason: Founders often include relevant links in pitch decks; scraping those directly is faster and more accurate than relying on Serper to find them

decision: Intent classification runs after KG traversal completes, not in parallel, so judge has access to the actual chunks extracted from documents
reason: Judge needs to read the real document content to extract proper nouns and ground the intent; running before traversal would force judge to work blind

decision: Judge prompt explicitly forbids using bare company name in search queries; must anchor on proper nouns (founder names, product names, etc.) extracted from KG
reason: Bare company names like 'Leaps' are too generic and hit unrelated results; proper nouns are specific and lead to correct web results

decision: Per-cell chat should never lock based on project-level session status; only show brief confirmation flash on Submit
reason: Project-level `submitted` flag is too coarse-grained; it was preventing analysts from continuing conversation in any cell after group consensus, blocking iterative refinement

decision: Cross-cell context transfer happens via RAG retrieval of KG-stored Q&A, not explicit chat history injection
reason: Explicit upstream context only from same cell's prior analysis (`output_cache`); implicit transfer via semantic similarity search is more flexible and doesn't require explicit cell ordering
